sections.html:
Jacksonville is a Pulaski County city roughly 17 miles northeast of downtown Little Rock, inside the greater Little Rock area. The city has held near 30,000 people for about thirty years, with 29,477 counted in 2020 and 29,460 estimated now. Buyers tend to be local families, military households, or commuters who work elsewhere in the metro.

In 2020 the census listed 12,738 housing units, and 10.1 percent were vacant. Owner-occupied homes were rarely empty (2.2 percent vacancy) while 10.5 percent of rentals sat vacant. In plain terms, rentals turn over faster than owned homes, and a landlord with an empty unit should plan around that.

Jacksonville grew from 2,474 residents in 1950 to 14,488 in 1960, a surge that coincided with the air base opening. A big share of today's houses were built in that boom. Most are now older than fifty years, and inspectors tend to focus on roofs, wiring, plumbing and foundations. When an owner faces a long repair list, an as-is sale is often the sensible alternative.

Before you list, ask a roofer and an electrician for a quick look and write down what they find. Even if you decide not to fix anything, a written list of known issues lets a buyer price the house fairly and avoids last-minute renegotiation. If you sell to a cash buyer, the same list lets them make a firm offer sooner.

sections.h2: How the air base shapes demand
sections.html:
Little Rock Air Force Base, inside Jacksonville on 6,217 acres, is the Defense Department's primary C-130 training base. More than 3,300 people live on it and about 7,200 work there, which makes it the fourth-largest employer in Arkansas. Nothing else moves the local market as much.

  • Crews in training and permanent staff keep rentals and purchases moving.
  • New orders can force a sale with very little notice.
  • Service members who leave often keep the house as a rental or sell with a tenant in it.

If a move is urgent, a cash sale's certainty and speed may beat a higher asking price that takes months to collect.

The Jacksonville Museum of Military History preserves part of the area's wartime story, and the guard house of the old Arkansas Ordnance Plant is on the National Register of Historic Places. Both are easy local details to mention to a buyer who is new to the area.

sections.h2: The AICUZ overlay near the base
sections.html:
An overlay zoning district known as AICUZ places land-use limits on property around the air base, mainly near the flight paths. The city adopted it by ordinance in 1999, and it covers the Clear Zone plus Accident Potential Zones I and II. Within it, the city code allows no more than one single-family dwelling per acre, bars uses that expose people to noise above DNL 75 dB, and calls for sound insulation in new construction. Existing uses can continue, and a building rebuilt after damage may stay if its main use is the same.

Owners, title insurers and lenders get notice through a certified copy of the ordinance filed with the Pulaski County Circuit Clerk, Real Estate Division. If your street is near the base, a call to the title company or city planners will tell you whether the overlay reaches your lot. Make that call before you fix a closing date.

On March 31, 2023, an EF3 tornado with peak winds of 165 mph came through Jacksonville and damaged Dupree Park and the First Assembly of God Church. Lenders and inspectors can turn up a patched roof, an open insurance claim or an unfinished permit. Selling as is skips many of those questions. Even so, tell buyers about damage you know of.

After voters chose to leave the Pulaski County Special School District, Jacksonville North Pulaski School District became independent on July 1, 2016. It operates six elementary schools, Jacksonville Middle School and Jacksonville High School. Parents will ask which zone your house is in, so know the answer.

Buyers also mention Dupree, Fireman, Excell, Galloway, Johnson, Paradise, Northlake and Stagecoach parks, the Bayou Meto Urban Canoe Trail and Reed's Bridge Battlefield Heritage Park.

Tax is paid a year in arrears, so the October 15 deadline falls in the year after assessment. The base is 20 percent of market value, and a homestead's taxable value is held to a 5 percent annual rise until it catches up to the full assessed figure. Act 139 of 2023 sets a four-year reappraisal cycle.

The state adds a real property transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on deeds over $100. People recording a deed who are not attorneys, brokers, lenders or government representatives must show a photo ID.

Overdue real estate tax builds interest. Request the current balance from the county treasurer's office while you are still comparing offers. Your title company will deduct it from what you receive at closing. If your mortgage payments have slipped, get a payoff statement from the lender as well, so you can see what the sale must cover.

Once an offer is signed, the title company verifies ownership, searches for liens and drafts the settlement statement. That statement shows the mortgage payoff, any tax owed, the tax split between you and the buyer, and the transfer tax. The deed is then recorded at the Real Estate Department in Little Rock. With a cash buyer there is no loan approval or lender appraisal, so the date depends mostly on how quickly title is cleared.

Your three routes are a listing, a sale by owner and a cash offer. A listing suits a house in good condition when you can sit through showings, inspections and a buyer's loan approval. A cash sale gives up some of that upside for speed and fewer conditions.

  • With a tenant: a cash buyer can often take the house with the lease in place.
  • With an inherited house: confirm who holds title and whether probate must finish first.
  • With storm or age repairs: an as-is sale spares you the repair list.

Whichever route you pick, bring the deed, a photo ID, your latest tax statement and your lender's payoff figure to the first conversation. If the house is inherited, add the probate paperwork. If tenants live there, add the lease and the current rent.

faqs.a: The 2025 estimate is 29,460 residents, almost unchanged from the 29,477 counted in 2020.

faqs.q: Does Little Rock Air Force Base affect home values in Jacksonville?
faqs.a: It affects demand and some land-use rules. The AICUZ overlay limits development near the base, so a title company can tell you whether your lot is inside it.

faqs.q: Who handles my deed and tax bill?
faqs.a: Pulaski County bills the tax. Deeds are recorded by the Real Estate Department of the Pulaski Circuit and County Clerk.

faqs.q: What are the property tax deadline and late penalty?
faqs.a: Pay by October 15 of the year after assessment or face a 10 percent penalty. Overdue real estate tax also gathers interest, so ask the county for the exact payoff before you close.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Jacksonville house with storm damage?
faqs.a: Yes, as is. Keep repair and insurance records, and disclose damage you know about.
